faqHeading.title: Frequently asked questions.
faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for choosing industrial TVOC sensing, planning the monitoring points and connecting the data.

faqs.question: Which VOCs can this TVOC sensor measure?
paragraphs: Start with the chemical names, CAS numbers and expected mixture. The sensing configuration must be checked against those compounds. For PID configurations, response depends on lamp energy and chemical response factors; a PID does not identify each component of an unknown mixture. Ask for the selected sensor's compatibility and calibration information.

faqs.question: How is TVOC different from a gas-specific reading or %LEL?
paragraphs: TVOC provides an overall response to detectable compounds, while a gas-specific measurement targets an identified substance. %LEL describes flammable-gas concentration relative to its lower explosive limit. These measurements support different decisions. Compound-specific exposure assessment also uses defined averaging periods, so a mixed TVOC value alone cannot establish occupational exposure compliance.

faqs.question: Does 1 ppb resolution mean 1 ppb accuracy?
paragraphs: Resolution describes the smallest reported increment. Accuracy describes how closely the result agrees with the reference concentration; detection limit and response time are additional specifications. Ask for those values for the selected configuration, target gas and operating conditions when evaluating your application.

faqs.question: How do I specify an explosion-proof TVOC sensor for my site?
paragraphs: Share the site's area classification, required approval and installation conditions. Review the ordered equipment's Ex marking, certificate scope, ambient limits and any special conditions against those requirements. Include the gas or dust group, temperature class and the complete power, enclosure and accessory configuration. Have the site's responsible engineer confirm suitability before installation.

faqs.question: Where should a fixed TVOC sensor be installed, and how many do I need?
paragraphs: Place monitoring points using an assessment of release sources, vapor dispersion, airflow, obstructions and the purpose of the measurement. A point sensor reports the air at its location, so there is no universal coverage radius or mounting height. Have a qualified site engineer set the layout, and allow access for inspection and calibration.

faqs.question: How should calibration and maintenance be planned?
paragraphs: Use the instructions for the ordered sensing element. Agree the calibration gas, reference basis, function checks and service intervals before commissioning. Dust, contamination and operating conditions can change performance. For PID configurations, lamp condition and the applied response factor also matter. Keep calibration and inspection records for each monitoring point.

faqs.question: How do I choose TVOC thresholds and use remote alerts?
paragraphs: Base thresholds on the process, target compounds, calibration basis and monitoring objective. Establish normal operating readings and define who investigates an alert and what action they take. Test the complete notification path during commissioning. Reassess the settings when solvents, ventilation or the process change.

faqs.question: How do reporting intervals affect power demand and alert timing?
paragraphs: Sensing, reporting and notification timing are separate requirements to confirm. Faster sampling or transmission increases power demand; weak coverage and retries also extend update timing. Confirm the selected sensing configuration's supply requirements, including PID operation where specified. Verify end-to-end update and alert timing during commissioning.

faqs.question: How do I choose LoRa, 4G LTE or NB-IoT for an industrial site?
paragraphs: Check coverage at the mounting point and agree the destination platform, required update interval and integration responsibilities. Cellular configurations list MQTT support. For LoRa projects, confirm the gateway, network and payload requirements with the quotation. Record these details in the deployment plan so commissioning can verify data delivery.

faqs.question: What information should I send for a TVOC monitoring quotation?
paragraphs: Send the chemical list or SDS, expected concentrations, monitoring objective, number and locations of points, temperature and humidity, mounting and enclosure needs, wireless coverage and required update timing. For a classified location, add the area classification and required approval. Include the receiving platform and any project documentation requirements.
